what_happened: The route said to go straight, and the human drove straight on (green line). The policy's planned path (orange) instead bent left into the next lane while speeding up from 4.4 to 6.6 m/s. The ego's front cut into car 56, which was driving alongside in that left lane, by 7.2 s. The camera view was clean until the moment of impact, and the rear contact came only after this front collision.

On a multi-lane freeway at about 8 m/s, with plenty of room to the car ahead (~26 m), the policy planned a drift to the left toward the next lane. Its front-left corner then hit actor 33, which was coming up alongside in that left lane. At impact the ego was angled left and about 0.9 m left of the human's path.

After handoff the ego sped up from 4.4 to 6.7 m/s and drifted left out of its lane toward the lane where actor 15 was, while the recorded path went straight and then bore right. Its front hit actor 56, which was driving next to it in the left lane, about 1.5 m off the recorded path.

Driving straight in heavy freeway traffic after handoff, the ego sped up from 4.4 to 6.4 m/s and drifted left, about 1.5 m off the recorded path, into the adjacent lane. Its front-left corner hit actor 56, which was alongside and slightly ahead in that lane. A rear contact was also logged, but the front/side collision started first.

The ego was holding its lane on the freeway at about 8 m/s, staying within 0.9 m of the recorded human path. Actor 33 came up from behind in the lane to the left, passed the ego and moved right into the ego's lane just ahead of it, so its rear-right corner hit the ego's front-left corner, which is why the contact is scored as a front collision.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego drifted about 3 m left of the recorded path, ending up straddling the lane line behind actor 87, which was nearly stopped. The ego held about 6 m/s while the gap closed from 14 m to 2.4 m, and its front hit 87's rear-right corner. (An earlier rear contact by another actor also happened, but the at-fault failure is this front collision.)

The ego stayed about one lane left of the recorded path, which shifted right, and held about 6 m/s while closing on slower actor 87 ahead in that lane. The gap shrank from 14.4 m to 2.2 m with almost no braking, and the ego's front ran into 87. The ego was rear-ended earlier, but that played no part in this front collision.

The ego drove about one lane left of the recorded path and held about 6 m/s while closing on slower actor 87 ahead in its lane, with the gap shrinking from 14.5 m to 2.4 m. It never braked and hit 87 with its front at 10.6 s. The earlier rear contact came before this, and 87 looks smeared in the camera but is still clearly visible.

The ego had drifted about 3 m left of the recorded path, into the lane to its left, even though the command was RIGHT. It then held about 6.5 m/s while the gap to the slower actor 87 ahead in that lane shrank from 16.5 m to 3.7 m, and it hit 87's rear with its front without braking. Nearby cars in the camera view were smeared, but 87 could still be seen as a vehicle, so this does not explain the failure to brake.

Lead vehicle 9 appeared right in front of the ego around handoff (gap fell from 43.6 m to 0.5 m, overlapping at 5.2 s). After separating to about 8 m at 6.2 s, the nearly stopped vehicle 9 was closing fast, but the ego only eased from 5.4 to 4.5 m/s and drove into its rear at 7.2 s.

Actor 9 was already overlapping the ego's front in the ego's lane right at handoff (gap 0.5 m at 4.7 s; front contact in the 5.2 s frame), so the run started in a bad state. The gap then opened to about 8 m, but the ego held about 5.5 m/s and slowed only to 4.3 m/s, closed back in on the slower car and hit it again at 7.2 s. At that moment the ego was only 0.1 m from the recorded human path and the camera shows actor 9 as a smeared blob. Both suggest actor 9's reconstructed track may not match the real drive.

At handoff (4.7 s), actor 9 was already sitting on top of the ego: the gap was 0.5 m, and the 5.2 s frame shows the boxes overlapping. Actor 9 then pulled about 8 m ahead and stopped abruptly, and the ego, braking only mildly (5.5 to 4.3 m/s), ran back into it at 7.2 s. The ego was only about 0.2 to 0.9 m from the human's recorded path, so the human car would also have overlapped actor 9. In the camera, actor 9 looks like a see-through smeared ghost, which suggests a bad replayed track rather than a real lead vehicle.
